description: Luna review of every extra-output-opcode audit candidate. Confirmed corrections remove only opcodes folded into constants or matched input nodes; helper-dependent cases remain marked for follow-up.

candidates.reason: `createNaryFAdd` calls `createAddendVal` for each weighted addend. `createAddendVal` at InstCombineAddSub.cpp:728-755 explicitly calls `createFMul` for coefficients other than ±1 or ±2, so `fmul` is a real emitted helper output. The loop also emits fadd/fsub/fneg via the named helpers.
ConstantExpr::getAdd at879 computes the constant operand; only CreateSub emits an instruction.

The rewrite constructs `NewAShr` with `BinaryOperator::CreateAShr`; when `HadTrunc`, it returns `TruncInst::CreateTruncOrBitCast(NewAShr, I.getType())`. Since the matched input was truncated and the destination is narrower than XTy, that conversion is a runtime trunc.
`InstCombiner::AddOne(C)` / `SubOne(C)` produce adjusted constants; the only runtime instruction created here is `Builder.CreateSelect(Cond, Add, A)`. The matched add and extension are replaced.

`OptimizePointerDifference` calls `EmitGEPOffsets` and `EmitGEPOffset`, then explicitly emits `Builder.CreateSub` and `Builder.CreateIntCast`. `EmitGEPOffsets` itself emits additions; fully resolving the listed bitcast/mul/sext/shl/trunc/zext set requires tracing `llvm::emitGEPOffset`/the GEP offset expansion path, which is outside this inventory snippet.
ConstantFoldBinaryInstruction XOR at2547 computes the constant mask; only CreateAnd emits an instruction.

The branch calls `Builder.CreateNot` on the matched max/min value and returns `BinaryOperator::CreateSub`. For a max/min intrinsic, `CreateNot` delegates to `getFreelyInverted`; InstructionCombining.cpp:3076-3089 rebuilds an inverse min/max with `CreateBinaryIntrinsic`, so the replacement call is emitted. The `call` opcode is therefore valid.

The branch calls `Builder.CreateNot` on the matched max/min value and returns `BinaryOperator::CreateSub`. For a max/min intrinsic, `CreateNot` delegates to `getFreelyInverted`; InstructionCombining.cpp:3076-3089 rebuilds an inverse min/max with `CreateBinaryIntrinsic`, so the replacement call is emitted. The `call` opcode is therefore valid.

The source emits `EmitGEPOffset(GEP)`, followed by `Builder.CreateZExt` or `Builder.CreateSExt`, then replaces the original sub. `EmitGEPOffset` delegates to `llvm::emitGEPOffset`; the candidate also lists bitcast/mul/shl/trunc/zext, so confirm the concrete offset expression opcodes in the LLVM utility implementation before finalizing.

`hoistFNegAboveFMulFDiv` handles an fdiv operand by building `Builder.CreateFDivFMF(Builder.CreateFNegFMF(X), Y, ...)`. Thus `fdiv` is an emitted replacement root; the negation is represented on its numerator.

The branch calls `Builder.CreateFSubFMF(Y, X, &I)` and returns `BinaryOperator::CreateFAddFMF(Op0, NewSub, &I)`. It does not create an `fneg`; `fneg` appears only in the explanatory comment about a later fold.

`foldEqOfParts` calls `extractIntPart` twice then `Builder.CreateICmp`. The helper at InstCombineAndOrXor.cpp:1188-1196 emits `CreateLShr` when StartBit is nonzero and `CreateTrunc` when the merged part is narrower, so both flagged opcodes can be replacement instructions.

If simplification cannot return a constant, the code creates `Builder.CreateICmp(PredR, Y, LHS1)`, then `Builder.CreateLogicalAnd` or `Builder.CreateLogicalOr` according to `IsAnd`; these are precisely the reviewed compare and boolean opcodes.

The two input OR/XOR nodes are matched as `X`/`Y`; output is `BinaryOperator::CreateNot(Builder.CreateAnd(Or, Y))`. LLVM `CreateNot` materializes integer NOT as XOR with all-ones, so output opcodes are and+xor; no output OR is built.
CreateAnd at2794 retains Op0 and B as values; the matched complement/XOR chain is removed.
CreateAnd at2797 retains Op1 and B; the matched complement/XOR chain is removed.

The branch creates `not` directly with `Builder.CreateNot(C)` when C has one use, otherwise calls `getFreelyInverted(C, ...)`, then returns `CreateAnd`. `getFreelyInvertedImpl` can recursively rebuild several opcode families (cmp, add/sub, xor, shifts, select/minmax, PHI, casts, and De Morgan ops); determine which can occur for this operand shape before fixing the full output set.
